Thanks Liam / Sophie — received and reviewed briefly. Quick summary of Redwood's position and next steps below: 

- Delegation / processor-to-processor: Redwood is generally ok with a delegation clause but needs: (a) subprocessor roster and ability to enforce contractual flow-down; (b) right to approve high-risk subprocessors; (c) explicit security controls and breach notification SLAs in the chain.
- SCCs: we prefer the standard Commission SCCs template and can execute via Annex A (controller-processor) or Annex B (processor-processor) depending on roles. The "Annex II alternative" will need legal review — our privacy counsel has concerns about the choice impacting import/export obligations.
- Export controls / TIA: we will kick off a TIA. This will require input from Security (evidence on encryption at rest/in transit) and from infra on region routing. Expect 3–5 business days for a preliminary impact note.

Action items I am assigning here:
  1) Monica to coordinate subprocessor evidence and update the roster (monica.patel@redwood.ai)
  2) Karthik to lead legal redline negotiation on SCC selection and liability carve-in (karthik.iyer@redwood.ai)
  3) Mina to confirm SLA windows for breach notifications and whether we can accept the limited carve requested (mina.haddad@redwood.ai)

We'd like to propose a short call tomorrow to go through the redlines with DataHealth legal and Orrin & Co. Are you available 9:00–11:00am BST?

Best,

On Thu, 19 Jun 2025 at 09:16, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Mina / Karthik — per your ask, pulled the current subprocessor roster and prepared an evidence pack...

Team / DataHealth legal — thanks for patience. Quick positions Redwood is prepared to take in negotiation: 
1) Delegation: Acceptable if DataHealth agrees to (a) Redwood right to approve high-risk subprocessors; (b) flow-down security commitments; and (c) contract exhibit with current roster updated within 10 business days of signature.
2) SCCs: Redwood will execute the EU Commission SCCs and sign as processor where applicable. We will not accept a bespoke Annex II alternative without further counsel sign-off; if DataHealth prefers Orrin's proposed path, Orrin please provide a short memo on legal implications for cross-border processing so we can advise.
3) Liability / breach carve: Redwood cannot accept an open-ended carve that pushes controller-level liability to Redwood. We are willing to accept a narrow cooperation clause with defined SLA (48 hours initial notification to customer) and a negotiated cap to apply to breach-related liabilities tied to Redwood's proven fault.

Escalation request: if DataHealth insists on Annex II or the broader liability carve, we will need an exception approval from VP Legal and the CRO. Please flag any clauses you consider non-starter so we can escalate earlier.

Next step: propose a 45-minute negotiation call Monday 23 Jun 2025 10:00 BST. Please confirm availability and whether Orrin can circulate their memo before the call.

Regards,
